headline: Longs lose $404M in four hours as BTC briefly breaks $80K and recovers; funding falls from 10% to 6.48%.
summary: Leveraged longs were flushed below $80K, yet options paid up for downside protection: the 30-day risk reversal widened from −3.43 to −4.82 while realized volatility sank to a 1-year low. ETFs saw a provisional further $138M outflow on Oct 23 and the STH in-profit share fell to 52.6%, so US spot demand is still absent. Bull day 16, no exit-framework trigger; watch the true market mean at $79,409 and the FOMC early on Oct 29 (Taipei).

points: Today's finding 1 (bearish) is in derivatives: longs washed out and funding fell while the risk reversal widened; finding 2 (neutral) explains that the Puell jump comes mostly from faster block production, not overheated valuation.

cycle.lead: Market phase: bull (since 2026-10-09, day 16), with 45 straight closes above a rising 200-day MA (threshold 30); evidence lights stay at 3/6.
points: The 200-day MA is $72,900, above $70,852 thirty days ago and still rising; capitulation has already occurred (2026-06-30, $58,525).

Evidence lights 3/6 (strength of evidence only, not part of the call): MVRV above its 1-year average (1.497 vs 1.427), realized cap +1.15% over 30 days, and close above the STH cost basis of $74,573 (Oct 18) are lit; 12-month momentum (−26.5%), 90-day exchange supply (+1.30%) and STH cost vs true market mean (−6.09%, Oct 18) are not.

Extrapolating the last 30 days linearly, the STH cost basis would cross above the true market mean around 2027-01-02 (prior estimate Dec 28); assuming a flat price, 12-month momentum would turn positive around 2027-01-31. Both are linear extrapolation / flat-price assumptions, not forecasts.
Falling back to bear requires 30 straight closes below a falling 200-day MA; days below it now: 0. Tidemark low test: no break of $58,525 before Dec 19.

news.title: BTC fell to about $79,280 intraday, breaking $80,000 for the first time since Oct 15; crypto longs lost $404M in four hours ($436M total) and $815M over 24 hours; futures OI −2.2%
news.read: Liquidations were concentrated in longs on Binance and Hyperliquid, and the site's OI-weighted funding fell from 10.08% to 6.48% at the same time, so part of the leveraged long book was washed out. The close recovered to $80,772, still above the true market mean of $79,409: a short-term deleveraging that does not change the market phase, though the area below $80K has now been tested twice.

It does not affect the cycle call, but if energy inflation makes the FOMC more hawkish, short-term volatility could widen.

findings.title: Longs flushed out; options now pay up for downside protection
findings.lean_why: Some leverage is gone, but options still bid up puts while realized volatility sits at a low, meaning traders see more downside than upside risk, and spot buyers have not stepped in.
findings.what: On Oct 24 BTC fell to $79,121 intraday (site's Kraken daily bar); The Block, citing CoinGlass: $404M of longs liquidated in four hours, $815M in 24 hours, futures OI −2.2%. OI-weighted funding fell from 10.08% to 6.48%; the 30-day 25Δ risk reversal widened from −3.43 to −4.82; RV30 24.98 (Oct 24), 1-year percentile 1.6, the lowest in 68 days.
findings.why: Breaking it down, the leverage side is retreating: the funding drop comes mainly from OKX (10.95% → 2.40%), while Hyperliquid is still 10.95% and Deribit 0%. Options did not relax: puts 39.22 vs calls 34.41, DVOL 37.93 (1-year percentile 25.2) slightly higher, same-source implied minus realized 13.06 points. Spot did not step in either: ETFs provisional −$137.9M on Oct 23, Coinbase premium 7-day average −0.123% (6.7th percentile on the site). Derivatives deleveraging and options hedging appearing together with weak spot: three kinds of data point the same way.
findings.alt: The wider risk reversal may also be event hedging ahead of the Oct 30 monthly expiry (35.1% of OI) and the Oct 29 FOMC, not necessarily bearish; RV30 is a 30-day window whose low reflects the narrow range since late September, and a single 2.44% daily range barely moves it. Liquidation totals are third-party tallies and vary widely with the time window.
findings.history: RV30 in the bottom 2% of its 1-year range happened only once in the past year (2026-08-13, +21.9% over the next 30 days, n=1): too few samples, background only; the last reading this low was 23.4 on Aug 17.
findings.so: With fewer leveraged longs, cascade-liquidation pressure on a further drop is smaller than in the prior edition; but with bearish options and weak spot, there is little short-term upward drive. Neither the market phase (bull day 16) nor the exit framework is affected.
findings.next: By Oct 30: a risk reversal below −6 would mean hedging demand is deepening (confirm); a move back above −3 would mean demand for downside protection is fading (refute).

findings.title: Puell hits a 1-year high on faster blocks, not overheating
findings.lean_why: Miner revenue well above its 1-year average usually raises miners' incentive to sell, but this time it comes mostly from faster blocks and a falling 1-year average, and valuation metrics did not heat up.
findings.what: CoinMetrics Puell multiple on Oct 23: 1.2611, 1-year percentile 99.2, the highest in 18 days (last Oct 5 at 1.34); its 4-year percentile jumped from 39.8 to 75.5, 7-day average 1.1165.
findings.why: Puell = daily miner issuance revenue ÷ its 1-year average. Price did not push it up: the close is around $80K, 12-month momentum is −26.5%, and fees are only 0.44% of miner revenue. What moved is block count: 7-day average hashrate 1,065.6 EH/s, +3.29% on the week, average block time 571 s (target 600), and the Oct 29 difficulty adjustment is estimated at +5.09%, so more blocks than usual are being mined each day before the retarget. Cross-check: MVRV Z (39.9) and NUPL (38.8) from the same provider did not heat up; only one of the top three is elevated.
findings.alt: The 1-year average in the denominator is falling as last October's high-price days roll out of the window, which also lifts Puell and will not disappear after the retarget. CoinMetrics daily issuance is itself noisy (Oct 17 0.99, Oct 20 1.22), so single-day readings carry a lot of noise. Tidemark's own Puell reading differs; different methodologies are not compared.
findings.history: In the past year Puell reached the 98th percentile or higher 4 times (2025-04-22, 2025-05-10, 2025-07-09, 2026-10-05), followed by +19.2%, +5.4% and +4.8% over 30 days, median +5.4% (same-period baseline +2.0%, n=4): too few samples, background only.
findings.so: The exit framework's top zone needs any two of the three at ≥ 80; only Puell is above 75, so the acceleration rule is still far off. Higher miner revenue gives miners more room to sell, but Hash Ribbons show no capitulation (59 days), so miners are not a source of pressure.
findings.next: By Oct 31: once blocks return to about 10 minutes after the retarget, a Puell 4-year percentile back below 60 would mean this was block-count noise (confirm).

items.title: Fasanara Digital + Glassnode: Q4 2026 Institutional Market Perspectives
items.points: BTC regained its three main on-chain cost bases after the August short squeeze, which the report calls a mark of a healthy bull market; it argues the data since August is more than short covering. No current key levels are given.
items.meaning: Consistent with the site's market phase (bull day 16, close above the STH cost basis of $74,573 and the true market mean of $79,409); but today's close is only +1.7% above the true market mean, so that cushion is shrinking.

items.title: Quantifying Support and Resistance: Proximity-Weighted CBD
items.points: Methodology: weights the cost-basis distribution by distance from spot (scaled by 30-day volatility) into support/resistance indices; recalls how a $83.6–85.4K resistance band in spring 2026 capped price before a drop toward the low $60Ks. No current levels given.
items.meaning: The same zone as the site's URPD $84–86K bucket of about 1.168M BTC (Oct 23), supporting the read of overhead supply near $84K; a methodology piece, not used as a basis for the current call.
